sprint: Image Studio's object extraction gains three things asked for together: mark out a search area so only that region is looked at, compose one new picture from the objects you pick, and a results view that is actually traversable. All three land in one change because they share the same grid and the same extraction pass.
task: MARK OUT A SEARCH AREA. extractSheet already accepted opts.crop in SOURCE pixels (tools/sheet-extractor/js/extractor.js:414, clamped at 443-446, echoed back at 534), so this needed no extractor change at all — only a marker UI and one option passed through. The crop-drag machinery is already tool-agnostic: _startCropDrag(clientX,clientY) and _screenToContent(clientX,clientY,imgW,imgH) never read _activeTool, so both are reused unchanged and mousedown simply routes to them while Cut Out Objects is the active tool. _extractArea IS DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM _cropRect. _refreshBgControls arms the destructive Keep This / Trash It pair off _cropRect, so marking out where to LOOK must never arm a control that TRIMS. _finishCropDrag was rewritten around a forExtract/commit split so one gesture can land in either place. A9 asserts the trim pair stayed disabled throughout the whole marking flow. COMPOSE ONE PICTURE. Each result card carries a tick; picking two or more reveals Make One Picture, which shelf-packs the picked cutouts into a single new picture and replaces the one on screen. The compositor works by hand in a raw Uint8ClampedArray and NEVER through a canvas, because canvas backing stores are premultiplied and round-tripping a cutout at partial alpha corrupts its RGB — the same reason _applyAllExtracted already reads each cutout from its own PngEncoder blob via FileReader. A TRAVERSABLE GRID. _renderExtractGrid was a flat wall of unlabelled tiles with no ordering aid and no size readout. Each result is now a card carrying its number, its pixel size and a pick tick, on a wider grid (minmax 56->84px, gap 6->8px, max-height 180->260px). The tick calls stopPropagation so unticking can never double as 'use this one' — B6 proves it — and B9 confirms tapping the tile image itself still replaces the picture as before. ONE DELETION: _lastMouseClientX() was orphaned by the _finishCropDrag rewrite. Verified via grep -rn (one hit, the definition itself) and removed, per this codebase's own 'if unused, delete completely' convention. FOUR TEST-SIDE FIXES, all disclosed, none an app bug, and every one STRENGTHENED rather than weakened: 1. A3 asserted .picture-studio-crop-box existed BEFORE any drag, but _ensureCropBox() builds it lazily inside _startCropDrag and so cannot exist yet. Relocated after the drag and grown from one condition to three (exists && shown && width > 10), which is a stronger claim: it proves marking an area genuinely goes through the same crop-drag machinery. 2. C8 clicked the Result view's 'Looks Great', but _composeExtracted calls _toggleActiveTool(null) and never _setView, so the modal is still in the Edit view — the correct target is the footer's own .picture-studio-save-btn. 3. C8 and D4 both expected a bare data-URL string. The long-established contract for BOTH onApply and onApplyMany is {dataURL, width, height, imageView} (_bake, line 3208; _applyAllExtracted, line 1874). Both assertions now check the whole shape. 4. D4 additionally read m.dataUrl (lowercase 'rl') where the real field is m.dataURL. ONE FLAKE INVESTIGATED, NOT PAPERED OVER: image_studio_draw_verify.mjs timed out once on page.click('.picture-studio-cta-secondary'). A git stash A/B showed the baseline passing, which looked like a real regression — so rather than accept that, a dedicated in-page diagnostic probed all four Playwright actionability conditions WITH the changes applied: the button exists, is visible (offsetParent !== null), is enabled (disabled === false), has real geometry (180x44 at 702,746), is genuinely the top hit-target at its own centre (document.elementFromPoint returns the button itself), and is stable (byte-identical rects across two consecutive animation frames). The suite then passed 26/26 twice. Transient sandbox CPU-load flakiness; no code changed and no assertion weakened. Verified 35/35, zero page errors, via image_studio_extract_v2_verify.mjs (scratch-only) across five sections. A (12) is the search area, where A7 is decisive: with red marked out, exactly one object was found and blue was never looked at; A10/A11 confirm reset restores whole-picture search and A12 that leaving the tool clears the area. B (9) is the grid. C (8) is compose: the button appears only at two or more picked and withdraws at one, both colours appear in the composed canvas, the picture genuinely changed, the tool closed itself, the grid cleared, and the result applies back in the usual payload shape. D (5) guards the existing contracts — 'Use All' is still exactly one button, 'Make One Picture' cannot be mistaken for it, window.__many is an array of 2 in the usual shape, and the single-picture callback was not also fired. E (1) is zero page errors. The suite could not reach closure-private _stageRect/_state/_canvas to drag a box, so screenBoxOf() scans the RENDERED canvas for a target colour's bounding box and converts through the element's own getBoundingClientRect() — which is a truer test anyway, since it drags where the user would actually see the thing. Full regression, all eight suites green: image_studio_extract_verify 46/46 (the most at-risk, since this ship rewrites both _renderExtractGrid and _finishCropDrag), bg_default_verify 12/12, image_studio_draw_verify 26/26 (twice), crop_fix_verify 23/23, photo_via_studio_verify 8/8, fa_replace_everywhere_verify 22/22, and both goldenBuild suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS. renderer/slideRenderer.js is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust ?v=0360 -> ?v=0361 across all 59 tags. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder change — tools/world-builder/ and tools/world-builder-v2/ are completely untouched; confined to js/pictureStudio.js, css/style.css and index.html.
